model.name: Deploy-integrity: the served==committed / version guard covers only the SERVER half — client dist serves statically and goes live unversioned on build (guard-coverage gap, DEFERRED)
model.description: DEPLOY-INTEGRITY FINDING (PO capture 2026-08-31, DEFERRED pending Tron). The version-bump / served==committed / phantom guard protects only the SERVER HALF of a deploy. MECHANISM (PO/expert explanation, almost-certainly): dist is BUILT INTO THE WORKTREE and served STATICALLY, so CLIENT changes go live the instant they are BUILT (no restart needed) while SERVER changes wait for a RESTART. OBSERVED (PO/tester-measured): the 'source not available' CLIENT marker rendered on served 0.8.151 while the expert had that marker in the HELD v0.8.152 = prod was briefly serving 0.8.152 CLIENT code under a 0.8.151 VERSION STRING. So the version string + phantom guard track the SERVER half; a client change can be live-and-unversioned. The restart to v0.8.152 resolved THIS instance (PO-measured). ★ STATE IT AS WHAT IT IS: a GAP IN GUARD COVERAGE (the guard silently covers only half of what it claims), NOT a bug in anyone's work. A guard that covers half of what it claims = phantom-coverage one level up (R37.31 family). DEFERRED; nobody fixes now (functionality first); written down while we understand it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The served==committed / version guard covers BOTH the server AND the client half of a deploy: a client change live in dist under an old version string is DETECTED, not silently unversioned. Today it covers server-only.
The served CLIENT bundle's version is measurable/asserted independently of the server version, so 'client 0.8.152 under server 0.8.151' surfaces rather than reading as 0.8.151 everywhere.
Recorded as a GUARD-COVERAGE GAP (the guard's claim overstates its coverage), NOT a defect in the expert's deploy or anyone's work. The v0.8.152 restart resolved the instance; the gap is structural.
DEFERRED pending Tron scheduling; no work starts until scheduled (functionality-first).
The gap is evidenced by measuring served-client-marker vs served-server-version (as PO/tester did), not asserted; a client/server version skew is measurable.
